newsitem.title: FRANCE: French union blasts Elf, to widen refinery protest.
newsitem.headline: French union blasts Elf, to widen refinery protest.

text.p: France's largest trade union on Tuesday condemned a decision to assemble talks on an Elf Aquitaine refinery strike as a gimmick and said disruption by oil workers would soon spread to Shell and Esso plants.

The Socialist-backed CFDT said Elf Aquitaine had refused in preliminary talks on Tuesday to open negotiations on the strikers' real concerns about employment and was simply trying to buy time by bringing forward an ordinary pay round.
Elf's three French refineries have been closed for six days in a conflict triggered by planned job cuts and workers were due to vote by Wednesday morning on whether to keep up the strike.
Elf's refining subsidiary Elf Antar France said earlier that negotiations over pay and working organisation and conditions would start on Thursday at 1300 GMT.
"The company is simply trying to buy an end to the conflict by bringing forward the annual negotiation on salaries to December 5," the CFDT said in a statement.
"This is a manoeuvre that will not divert the staff, nor the CFDT, from their main objective of maintaining employment."
Unions have called for Elf to abandon plans to shed around 300 jobs or 10 percent of the staff at Elf Antar and have drawn up a list of further demands including early retirement.
Industry sources said the agenda for Thursday's negotiation appeared to leave the door open to discussion of early retirement but not a withdrawal of the job cuts plan.
In its statement, the CFDT gave further details of disruption planned at Shell and Esso refineries, first outlined by a union official earlier on Tuesday.
It said protests had been called from December 6 to December 10 at the 80,000 barrels-per-day Reichstett refinery near Strasbourg, eastern France, 65-percent owned by Shell France.
BP France, Elf, Total and Mobil also have stakes in the plant.
The CFDT said Shell's main French refineries at Berre in the south and Petit Couronne in the north would be hit by action on December 10. It called for all employees to take part.

It said talks were speeding up between France's five main unions on plans to disrupt Esso France plants next week. Like Elf, the Exxon Corp subsidiary has also announced plans to axe 10 percent of its French refinery staff.
The union did not say whether any of these extra protests would involve strike action, but a senior union official said earlier he thought there could be strikes.
None of the companies was immediately available for comment.
Previous disruption at Shell and Mobil in France in the past 10 days has been limited to isolated go-slows at two plants.
Unions are trying to win support for widespread protests by oil workers against a raft of reorganisations and cost-cutting in the refining sector, which has chronic overcapacity.
